edges.note: Two firmware slots with an atomic boot switch are the device-local form of blue-green's active/idle environment switch.
The intact inactive slot is the preserved prior state; failed boot falls back to it, mechanizing deployment rollback.
The validate-then-jump (SP/PC load, vector relocation) sequence is the mechanism the boot-stage structure depends on.
The split image layout fixes the handoff's entry address, stack-pointer source, and vector-table relocation.

edges.cite: POSA2 (Schmidt et al.), Half-Sync/Half-Async: known uses cite BSD-style top-half/bottom-half interrupt processing as the pattern's canonical OS instance
edges.note: ISR = async layer, deferred task-level completion = sync layer, queue between them.

edges.cite: Simon, An Embedded Software Primer, ch.5: ISRs enqueue function pointers that the main loop dequeues and runs - the architecture is this mechanism systematized
edges.note: The deferral queue is the architecture's defining structure.
The minimal ISR is the pattern's first half; deferred task-level completion is its second.
The HAL layer is composed of device drivers presenting hardware-independent interfaces.
A BSP definitionally packages the board's device drivers alongside boot and configuration code.
User-space NIC drivers move packets via DMA descriptor rings; without DMA there is no bypass path.
DMA masters bypass CPU memory protection, so ARINC-653-style partitioned systems must restrict or mediate DMA to preserve space partitioning.
Design-level instance of the adaptor connector: converts the interface a device offers into the one the application expects.

edges.cite: Douglass, Design Patterns for Embedded Systems in C, Hardware Adapter pattern: adapts the interface offered by a Hardware Proxy to the client's expected interface
edges.note: Adapter sits in front of the proxy.
Per-device proxies are the building blocks from which the hardware abstraction layer is assembled.
The encapsulate tactic at the hardware boundary: register layout and encodings hidden behind an explicit device-neutral interface.

edges.cite: Kopetz, Real-Time Systems: event-triggered systems initiate communication and computation on event occurrence signaled by interrupts
edges.note: Interrupt-driven activation is the ET style's load-bearing mechanism.
ISRs are the only asynchronous element the superloop structure admits; latency-sensitive work depends on them.
The hardware dispatch table through which interrupt-driven (event-triggered) activation reaches handler code.
The table's entries are ISR entry points; together they form the interrupt dispatch mechanism.
ISO/IEC TR 18037's standardized iord/iowr interface is the standards tactic applied to device-register access.
Isolates register access from the platform, forming the lowest sublayer of a HAL.
Volatile register access is the primitive every HAL driver is built on.
C++ template idiom realizing register access with compile-time legality checking at zero runtime cost.
Compile-time-checked register interfaces are used to build HAL layers in modern C++ firmware.
PID is the canonical controller computation inside the feedback-control-loop style's controller element.
The hierarchy's lowest-level controllers execute regulation laws, classically PID loops.

edges.cite: Kopetz, Real-Time Systems: time-triggered systems observe the environment by periodic sampling (polling) rather than interrupts
edges.note: Sampling is the TT style's observation mechanism.
The superloop's defining mechanism: the endless main loop polls and services every task and device in turn.

edges.cite: White, Making Embedded Systems: polling vs interrupt-driven I/O presented as the two alternatives for noticing device events
edges.note: Classic embedded design tradeoff.
Standard HAL-driver technique for write-only and clear-on-read registers; keeps read-modify-write logic correct inside the layer.

edges.cite: Simon, An Embedded Software Primer, ch.5 round-robin architecture: names the endless polling loop both as code mechanism and whole-system organization
edges.note: Same-name/same-mechanism pair across realms.
Removes the integer-overflow fault class by construction - fault prevention for numeric code.
Public-key cryptography underlying authenticated encrypted channels is multi-limb modular arithmetic.

edges.cite: Bass et al., Software Architecture in Practice, Exception Detection tactic: system exceptions include divide-by-zero and overflow detection
edges.note: Explicit overflow reporting is exception detection at the arithmetic level.
Alternative overflow policies (report vs clamp); Rust exposes checked_*/saturating_* variants side by side.
Comparing redundant channels' floating-point outputs requires tolerance comparison (the N-version 'consistent comparison' problem).
Voters over replicated numeric results must vote within an epsilon/ULP tolerance to avoid false divergence.
Replaces software floating-point emulation with integer instructions on FPU-less targets, cutting per-operation cost.
Guaranteed enclosures give a mechanical validity/reasonableness bound on computed outputs.
PoEAA base pattern; the canonical value-object building block for monetary quantities inside a Domain Model.
A seeded PRNG converts needed randomness into reproducible determinism - the standard mechanism for testable stochastic behavior.
Turns overflow - otherwise a fault - into a defined, handled case (clamp to range) within normal operation.
RFC 1982 wraparound-correct comparison keeps fixed-width sequence-number timestamps ordered across rollover.

edges.cite: Bass et al., SAIP, Schedule Resources tactic scheduling-policy discussion: names the cyclic executive as the static/offline scheduling strategy
edges.note: Offline-fixed dispatch order as a scheduling policy.

edges.cite: Kopetz, Real-Time Systems: time-triggered operating systems dispatch tasks from static (cyclic) schedules
edges.note: Node-level dispatch mechanism of TT systems.

edges.cite: Locke (1992), 'Software architecture for hard real-time applications: cyclic executives vs. fixed priority executives'
edges.note: The canonical comparison paper.

edges.cite: Google SRE book, 'Addressing Cascading Failures': deadline propagation described as the distributed form of per-stage timeouts
edges.note: Each stage enforces the propagated remaining budget as its timeout.
Suppresses responses to event edges arriving faster than the stability window - rate-bounding at the input boundary.
Hanmer's overload pattern: postponing low-importance work under load is event servicing by priority.

edges.cite: Bass et al., SAIP, Schedule Resources tactic: dynamic priority scheduling (incl. earliest-deadline-first) listed among the policies
edges.note: EDF as a named policy of the tactic.

edges.cite: Buttazzo (2005), 'Rate Monotonic vs. EDF: Judgment Day', Real-Time Systems 29(1): systematic comparison of the two policies
edges.note: Fixed vs dynamic priority tradeoff.
Constant-step simulation makes behavior reproducible independent of frame rate and hardware speed.
Client prediction and server reconciliation rely on deterministic fixed-step simulation both sides can replay.
Nygard's stability pattern: cap the rate of automated actions so automation cannot outrun human oversight.
A rate cap applied to automation's own actions rather than to inbound requests.
RTOS idle-task extension point for background and power-management work in task-based designs.
The canonical hook from which the CPU is put into low-power states when no task is ready.
Bounds the interrupt arrival rate at the CPU by batching events under a count/timeout policy.
Canonical traffic-shaping enforcement of a contracted arrival rate.
Admission control by constant-rate drain with overflow rejection.

edges.cite: Tanenbaum, Computer Networks, traffic-shaping section: presents leaky bucket and token bucket as the two alternatives
edges.note: Smooth constant rate vs bounded bursts.

edges.cite: Bass et al., SAIP, Schedule Resources tactic: round-robin named among the scheduling policies
edges.note: Fairness-oriented policy of the tactic.

edges.cite: Pont et al., 'Sandwich Delay' pattern (PLoP): equalizing code-section duration to reduce jitter in time-triggered embedded systems
edges.note: Jitter-control mechanism for TT schedules.

edges.cite: AUTOSAR OS specification: schedule tables provide statically configured time-triggered task activation on a counter
edges.note: The automotive TT activation mechanism.
Component-level embodiment of the tactic: an object applying an explicit scheduling policy to a contended resource.
Kernel timer service that task-based RTOS applications depend on for timeouts and periodic work.

edges.cite: Bass et al., SAIP, Schedule Resources tactic: fixed-priority scheduling (incl. rate-monotonic and deadline-monotonic) listed among the policies
edges.note: RMS/DMS as named policies of the tactic.
Definitional dependency: the style is decomposition into prioritized, preemptively scheduled RTOS tasks.
The tick interrupt is the kernel's time base, driving delays, timeslicing, and timeout detection.
Logical timers are multiplexed onto the single hardware tick.
Definitional match: execute at most once per interval, discarding or coalescing faster arrivals.
Same-name pair: the function-level rate-cap mechanism, applied at service scale, becomes admission-control throttling.
The two standard contrasted rate-control idioms for bursty input (fire at bounded rate vs fire after quiet period).
Suppresses periodic wakeups so the CPU stays in deep low-power states - the energy tactic applied to the scheduler tick.
Tickless entry/exit is typically driven from the idle task or its hook.
TTL is the standard staleness bound and invalidation contract that makes cached or replicated copies safe to use.

edges.cite: Pont, Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems: TTC schedulers presented as the implementation of time-triggered (Kopetz) system design
edges.note: The book's whole premise is this realization.
Tick-driven, table-dispatched variant of the non-preemptive run-to-completion executive.

edges.cite: Varghese & Lauck (1987), 'Hashed and Hierarchical Timing Wheels: Data Structures for the Efficient Implementation of a Timer Facility'
edges.note: The title states the relation: the data structure implementing a timer facility.
O(1) start/stop/expire in the critical path - Varghese-Lauck's stated motivation is timer-operation efficiency.
The canonical admission-control algorithm permitting bounded bursts within a sustained rate.
Enforces a contracted arrival rate and burst size - the SLA-policing mechanism of the tactic.

edges.cite: Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, runtime gameplay foundation systems: per-object updating is the core mechanism of the gameplay foundations layer
edges.note: Object updating drives the engine's top runtime layer.
Nystrom pairs Update Method with the Game Loop, whose timestep policy fixed timestep is; updates are driven per tick.
A decentralized scheduling policy balancing load across worker deques.
Actor runtimes (Akka's fork-join dispatcher, Erlang SMP schedulers) dispatch actors on work-stealing pools.

unbridged.why: Pure numerical-accuracy micro-technique; no architecture element (style, tactic, pattern) addresses silent floating-point precision loss - nearest tactic (exception-prevention) concerns fault classes, not rounding error.
